title.narrative: Women, Peace and Security High-Level Signatory Event: "Navigating 1325 in a New Security Reality"

description.narrative:
On 4th November 2025, the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) and the Ministry of Defense (MinDef), together with the Dutch gender platform WO=MEN, are organizing a high-level signatory event related to the Dutch National Action Plan (NAP) on Women Peace and Security (WPS) and the celebration of 25 years of resolution 1325 on WPS. This event, called "Navigating 1325 in a New Security Reality", brings together policy makers, military professionals, and civil society organisations.
This conference aims to: 1. Bridge: share 25 years of WPS experience and strengthen collaboration for inclusive peace, security and resilience in the face of current threats. 2. Inspire: sharpen understanding of how WPS can address today’s threats and strengthen resilience. 3. Equip: generate strategic insights and perspectives to face today’s new security and global reality.
The conference concentrates on a number of areas where WPS directly meets today’s security and global challenges, both in keynote speeches and via side-event sessions:
* Participation: ensuring women can fully and meaningfully shape peace and security decisions. * Gender Responsive Leadership: leading with courage, inclusion, and the conviction that diversity builds resilience. * Prevention: making the prevention of violence against women central to every security strategy. * Protection: addressing gender-based violence in conflicts with stronger prevention and response.
Deliverables: • A shared understanding of WPS in today’s security landscape. Participants will leave with a deeper and shared understanding of the strategic relevance of the Women, Peace and Security agenda in a rapidly changing geopolitical context, including the rise of hybrid threats, disinformation, and societal disruption. Also attention will be given to the increased use of gendered tactics of war, and how these impact resilience and security across sectors. • Practical insights and tools for policy and practice. Through cross-sector dialogue, the event will highlight best practices, lessons learned, and innovative responses from across the Dutch National Action Plan (NAP 1325) partnership. Participants will gain practical insights and tools to further integrate WPS across emerging policy domains and operational realities. • Visibility and mobilisation of WPS support. The event will reinforce the Netherlands’ role as a visible champion of WPS and inclusive security, and will strengthen collaboration across ministries, defense forces, and civil society. It may also provide a platform to introduce and promote the new Dutch WPS funding instrument, showcasing that targeted financial resources are available to support implementation and innovation in this field.
This conference is organized in the context of the Dutch NAP on WPS, of which the MFA is the co-coordinator. Through the discussions on WPS in today's security challenges, and the sharing of knowledge and experiences with a wide variety of stakeholders, this conference helps to improve the effective implementation of the WPS agenda and thereby contributes to the policy objectives of the MFA Taskforce Women's Rights and Gender Equality (TFVG).
